name: Question 3
problem: Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of ${sin}^{2}⁡(x)$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
worked_solution:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=a$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(a)}{4!}(x-a)^{4}.
$$

Here, we have $a=\frac{\pi }{2},$ so

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(\frac{\pi }{2})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})(x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{4!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}.
$$

So we need to work out $f(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and ${f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={sin}^{2}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{2}) & ={sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{2})=-2 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =-8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{2})=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${P}_{4}(x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =1+(0)(x-\frac{\pi }{2})+(\frac{(-2)}{2!}){(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{0}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+\frac{8}{4!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4} \\  & =1-{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of sin2⁡(x) about x=π2.

a
1+(x−π2)2+43(x−π2)4
b
1+4(x−π2)2−23(x−π2)4
c
1+2(x−π2)2−23(x−π2)4
d
1−(x−π2)2+13(x−π2)4
e
1−2(x−π2)2−13(x−π2)4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by

P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=π2, so

P4(x)=f(π2)+f′(π2)(x−π2)+f″(π2)2!(x−π2)2+f‴(π2)3!(x−π2)3+f(4)(π2)4!(x−π2)4.

So we need to work out f(π2), f′(π2), f″(π2), f‴(π2) and f(4)(π2), as follows:

f(x)=sin2⁡(x)⟹f(π2)=sin2⁡(π2)=1f′(x)=sin⁡(2x)⟹f′(π2)=sin⁡(2π2)=0f′(x)=2cos⁡(2x)⟹f″(π2)=2cos⁡(2π2)=−2f‴(x)=−4sin⁡(2x)⟹f‴(π2)=−4sin⁡(2π2)=0f(4)(x)=−8cos⁡(2x)⟹f(4)(π2)=−8cos⁡(2π2)=8

Therefore, P4(x) is given by P4(x)=1+(0)(x−π2)+((−2)2!)(x−π2)2+03!(x−π2)3+84!(x−π2)4=1−(x−π2)2+13(x−π2)4.
